ICON-2I forecasts (ItaliaMeteo-ARPAE)¶

Operational ICON-2I forecasts for Italy, run by Agenzia ItaliaMeteo with ARPAE-SIMC at about 2.2 km, with every variable of the deterministic run on surface and pressure levels. A new run is added twice a day (00 and 12 UTC starts) and runs are kept, so the store grows along init_time.

  • init_time: start of the run; lead_time: 0 to 72 h in hourly steps; valid_time = init_time + lead_time.
  • Surface and single-level variables (66) sit at the root of the store; temperature, wind, humidity, vertical velocity and geopotential height at 1000, 925, 850, 700, 500 and 250 hPa are in the pressure_level group.
  • Temperatures are in °C. Precipitation, runoff and the radiation and heat fluxes are average rates over the hour ending at each step (precipitation in kg m⁻² s⁻¹, i.e. mm/s), so they are NaN at lead time 0; multiply by 3600 for mm per hour.

Latest run¶

In [4]:
run = ds.isel(init_time=-1)
run_pl = pl.isel(init_time=-1)
str(run.init_time.values)[:16]
Out[4]:
'2026-10-07T00:00'

2 m temperature and 10 m wind at +24 h¶

In [5]:
step = np.timedelta64(24, "h")
t2m = run["temperature_2m"].sel(lead_time=step)
wind = run[["wind_u_10m", "wind_v_10m"]].sel(lead_time=step).isel(latitude=slice(None, None, 25), longitude=slice(None, None, 25))

ax = plt.figure(figsize=(9, 8)).add_subplot(projection=ccrs.PlateCarree())
t2m.plot(ax=ax, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), cmap="RdYlBu_r", robust=True, cbar_kwargs={"shrink": 0.7})
ax.quiver(wind.longitude, wind.latitude, wind.wind_u_10m, wind.wind_v_10m, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), scale=300, width=0.002)
ax.coastlines("50m")
ax.set_title(f"2 m temperature and 10 m wind, valid {str(t2m.valid_time.values)[:16]} UTC")
Out[5]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, '2 m temperature and 10 m wind, valid 2026-10-08T00:00 UTC')

Precipitation over the first 24 hours¶

The store holds the average rate over each hour, so a total is the sum of the hourly rates times 3600 s.

In [6]:
first_day = run["precipitation_surface"].sel(lead_time=slice(np.timedelta64(1, "h"), np.timedelta64(24, "h")))
total_mm = (first_day * 3600).sum("lead_time")

ax = plt.figure(figsize=(9, 8)).add_subplot(projection=ccrs.PlateCarree())
total_mm.where(total_mm >= 0.5).plot(ax=ax, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=60,
                                     cbar_kwargs={"label": "mm in 24 h", "shrink": 0.7})
ax.coastlines("50m")
ax.set_title("Precipitation, first 24 h of the run")
Out[6]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, 'Precipitation, first 24 h of the run')

Upper air: 850 hPa temperature and 500 hPa geopotential height¶

In [7]:
t850 = run_pl["temperature"].sel(pressure_level=850, lead_time=step)
z500 = run_pl["geopotential_height"].sel(pressure_level=500, lead_time=step)

ax = plt.figure(figsize=(9, 8)).add_subplot(projection=ccrs.PlateCarree())
t850.plot(ax=ax, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), cmap="RdYlBu_r", robust=True, cbar_kwargs={"shrink": 0.7})
lines = ax.contour(z500.longitude, z500.latitude, z500, levels=np.arange(5000, 6000, 40), colors="k",
                   linewidths=0.8, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree())
ax.clabel(lines, fmt="%d m", fontsize=8)
ax.coastlines("50m")
ax.set_title("850 hPa temperature, 500 hPa geopotential height (m)")
Out[7]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, '850 hPa temperature, 500 hPa geopotential height (m)')

Point meteogram — Rome¶

In [8]:
rome = dict(latitude=41.9, longitude=12.5, method="nearest")
point = run[["temperature_2m", "dew_point_temperature_2m", "precipitation_surface", "wind_gust_10m"]].sel(**rome)
valid = point.valid_time.values

fig, (a1, a2, a3) = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(10, 8), sharex=True)
a1.plot(valid, point.temperature_2m, label="temperature")
a1.plot(valid, point.dew_point_temperature_2m, label="dew point")
a1.set_ylabel("°C"); a1.legend()
a2.bar(valid, point.precipitation_surface * 3600, width=1 / 24)
a2.set_ylabel("mm / h")
a3.plot(valid, point.wind_gust_10m, color="tab:red")
a3.set_ylabel("gust, m/s")
for a in (a1, a2, a3):
    a.grid(alpha=0.3)
a1.set_title("ICON-2I forecast for Rome")
Out[8]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, 'ICON-2I forecast for Rome')

Relative humidity on the pressure levels over Rome¶

In [9]:
profile = run_pl["relative_humidity"].sel(**rome)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))
profile.plot(ax=ax, x="valid_time", y="pressure_level", cmap="GnBu", vmin=0, vmax=100, yincrease=False)
ax.set_title("Relative humidity over Rome (hPa levels)")
